doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Alcohol, Paris and the hit record
title: Drinking too much and not knowing music
summary: Moody says he drank heavily because people praised him though he knew no music and did not know he should practice.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Now, it wasn't too long after you left Dizzy that you became a leader, yourself, for the first time. Is that?
Well, I -- I came to -- well, first of all, I had a bout with alcohol. Okay? So I drank,
So you were in the part of the bus that -­
-- you were in the part of the bus that drank alcohol? [laughs]
Yeah, but I don't mean -- I'm not talking about the bus -­

-- but I mean, I just drank too much. And I know why I was drinking, now. The reason -- one of the reasons I was drinking was because -- well, first of all -- and -- and it lingered on till when I had my septet. And the reason was because people say, "Boy, you sound good." But I didn't know any music. You know what I mean? And -- because you're supposed to be going, but I -- you know, I said, "Damn! I." You know. "You sound good." "Yeah, but I." And I didn't know you were supposed to practice. I didn't know all those things. Believe it or not.
Even after all that time with Dizzy and being around the other musicians and seeing what they did and everything?
Oh, but you didn't see them. You went and played your thing and then you'd go another place.
